title: MVP: Model metadata schema v1 + automated customer-visible release notes/changelog generation
creator: Paula Mendes
project: Unified Rollouts: Model metadata + changelog generator
description:
Problem
- Today, model/version change information is split across the model registry, runtime config, and docs/release processes. Customers (and Support) often cannot answer: what changed, why, risk level, how to roll back, and where/when it’s available (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
- Enterprise/procurement increasingly requires customer-visible model change logs plus internal auditability (who changed what/when) and retention controls.

MVP objective
- Standardize a single metadata schema (v1) for all served models/variants/quantization profiles.
- Generate consistent, customer-visible release notes automatically from metadata + change events.
- Provide internal audit events + internal views/exports for Support/Security without leaking internal-only details to customers.

What’s in MVP (must-have)
1) Model metadata schema v1 (definition + validation + examples)
   - Required fields (v1):
     - model_id / variant_id (stable identifiers)
     - semantic_version (semver) for served model artifacts
     - deployment availability (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and gating flags (eligible/ineligible)
     - compatibility constraints (tokenizer, runtime, context length constraints, tool/function calling support, structured output constraints)
     - deprecation fields (status, timeline, replacement)
     - change risk classification + customer-facing summary fields
     - public vs internal field separation strategy (explicit)
   - Validation tooling in CI (schema validation + required fields + redaction tests)

2) Source of truth + publishing workflow
   - Source of truth: model registry record (schema v1) as the canonical store.
   - Control plane emits structured change events on edits/promotions/rollbacks/deprecations.
   - Changelog generator produces artifacts (public + internal views) with deterministic templating.

3) Changelog generator (initial GA)
   - Inputs: change events (preferred) + current metadata snapshot.
   - Outputs:
     - customer-visible release note entries (categorized: security, breaking, perf, quality, bugfix, deprecation)
     - internal audit-friendly entry that includes additional context (e.g., operator, internal ticket/PR refs) and is not exposed publicly.
   - Templating: stable language, severity, and “what you may notice / what to do” guidance.

4) Console integration
   - Per-model change history view (with filtering by deployment and time).
   - Release notes feed for rollouts/A-B surfaces (shows relevant notes during canary / experiments).
   - RBAC: ensure internal-only fields never render for non-admin roles.

5) Docs integration
   - Public release notes pages generated from changelog artifacts during docs build.
   - Basic routing/URLs and an index feed.

6) Audit logging (enterprise readiness)
   - Emit audit events for model metadata create/update/promote/rollback/deprecate.
   - Retention + SIEM export considerations documented; internal query endpoint for Support/Compliance.

Out of scope for MVP (explicit non-goals)
- Full historical backfill of all past model changes (do a small backfill only for 1–3 high-traffic models).
- Customer notification subscriptions (email/webhook) beyond basic internal webhook plumbing.
- Rewriting all legacy docs release notes.
- Making statistically strong, quantified “quality improved by X%” claims (MVP focuses on safe summaries + links to methodology).

Milestones (targeted)
- M0: Discovery/design alignment (complete)
  - Inventory fields currently in registry/runtime/docs
  - Agree on v1 fields + invariants + public/internal model
  - Confirm event types and minimal audit payload
- M1: Schema v1 + validation shipped (by 2025-10-25)
  - JSON schema (or equivalent) in model registry repo
  - CI validation + required check in release train
- M2: Registry migration + backfill (by 2025-11-08)
  - Backfill required v1 fields for existing catalog models
  - Rollback plan tested in staging
- M3: Eventing + generator + templates (by 2025-11-22)
  - Change events emitted and ingested
  - Deterministic artifact generation + public/internal filtering
- M4: Console + docs integration (by 2025-11-29)
  - Console endpoints + UI
  - Docs build consumes artifacts to render pages
- M5: Beta + launch readiness (by 2025-12-06)
  - 1–2 enterprise accounts dogfood/beta
  - Support playbook + FAQ draft
  - Security sign-off on audit/retention + redaction

Launch criteria (MVP = “GA-ready”)
Functional
- 95%+ of active hosted catalog models have v1 metadata with required fields populated.
- Every model version promotion produces a customer-visible release note entry within 10 minutes (p95 end-to-end pipeline).
- Console shows correct per-model history; filter by Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Docs site publishes release note pages and index reliably on deploy.

Safety / Security
- Hard guarantee: internal-only fields never appear in customer-visible surfaces (Console, docs, SDK).
  - Automated tests: snapshot tests for templating + redaction, RBAC UI tests, and a “deny-list” scanner on artifacts.
- Audit events emitted for create/update/promote/rollback/deprecate with consistent actor + request IDs.

Operational
- Runbook exists for:
  - correcting a bad public note (edit workflow + traceability)
  - rolling back a promotion
  - handling an incident where docs build publishes incomplete notes
- On-call ownership established for generator pipeline + docs build step (pager routing documented).

Success metrics (how we’ll know MVP worked)
- Reduce Support escalations where we cannot identify model change context (target: -30% over 60 days; baseline from SUP-28429 class of tickets).
- Coverage: release note entry present for >= 98% of promotions after GA.
- Time-to-answer for “what changed?” inquiries: from hours/days to < 15 minutes using Console + internal audit view.
- Enterprise procurement unblock: Northbridge + Lattice security review questions answered with concrete artifacts and retention posture.

Open questions
- Public “quality” notes: what qualifies as mention-worthy vs too noisy? (Need clear thresholds + language that avoids overstating.)
- Private deployment cadence: how do we represent staggered availability while keeping a single source of truth?
- Do we require explicit “customer impact” field for every promotion, or allow ‘none’?

Risks
- Redaction failures (highest severity): mitigated by deny-list scanner + RBAC regression tests + required reviewer check.
- Backfill incompleteness: mitigated by migration checklist + gating promotion on required fields.
- Pipeline reliability: docs build publishing incomplete notes; mitigated by artifact validity checks and “fail closed” behavior.

Notes
- This is a parent issue coordinating MVP across registry/control plane/generator/console/docs/security/support. Delivery is tracked via sub-issues listed above.
comments: 2025-09-24 (Marissa Cole): Aligning with Paula that this must be positioned as enterprise-readiness, not just docs polish. Northbridge explicitly asked for auditability + retention; release notes are the visible output but audit events are the procurement blocker.

2025-09-26 (Dylan Brooks): For Console MVP, we should ship the per-model change history view first even if the global feed is v0. Support needs a fast path to answer “what changed on account X?”—we can add per-account filtering later but need model history + timestamp + deployment now.

2025-09-29 (Naomi Feldman): Please ensure we have a crisp statement of what’s logged in audit events and what’s excluded. We should treat “internal note” fields as potentially sensitive; retention and export requirements will vary by deployment mode (Hosted vs Private).

2025-10-02 (Elliot Price): Docs side can consume JSON artifacts, but we need stable URL conventions and a guarantee that the generator produces an index page input. Also need an embargo mechanism for customer-specific items (even if MVP just supports internal-only notes).

2025-10-07 (Connor O’Brien): Release train: we can make “release note preview” a required check for registry changes and control-plane promotions. Strong preference for failing closed when required fields are missing or redaction rules fail. Proposed date to turn on required checks: 2025-11-04.

2025-10-10 (Chloe Martin): Support escalation from SUP-28429 showed we need a temporary internal export before UI is perfect. Suggest: internal admin endpoint + CSV/JSON export as stopgap; UI can follow without blocking support workflows.

2025-10-14 (Quentin Harris): Schema v1 should treat quantization profiles as first-class variants with their own semver and compatibility. We’ve had confusion where ‘same model’ behaves differently under quantization; release notes must be able to call that out without implying base weights changed.

2025-10-16 (Paula Mendes): For rollout policies, we need an explicit ‘rollout eligibility’ section in metadata: allowed deployments, canary eligible, A/B eligible, and any known regression risk flags. This should be a gating input to policy engine, not just descriptive.
updates: 2025-10-01: Scope and milestones reviewed with Eng leads; added explicit launch criteria around redaction guarantees + p95 generation latency.
2025-10-08: Added audit logging requirements as must-have (was previously ‘nice-to-have’).
2025-10-18: Updated dependencies/sub-issues list to include Private export ticket (ENG-9829) and PM-413 (beta selection + launch plan).
